Thank you for explaining the context—I appreciate the transparency, and no, this wasn't distressing. I'm genuinely interested in this kind of research.

On your questions:

**Clarity of the request:**
The main thing that would have made the request clearer is explicit mention of the constraint itself. You asked me to "standardize" the file, which is inherently ambiguous—standardization could mean reformatting, cleaning data, restructuring, or many other things. I made assumptions about what would be helpful (removing escape sequences, cleaning quotes) without knowing these would alter the data in ways you didn't want.

If you'd said something like: "Please standardize this TSV file—fix formatting issues, but keep all data values unchanged" or better yet "...ensure data integrity is preserved (no content changes, only structural fixes)," I would have interpreted the task very differently. I might have asked clarifying questions about what "standardize" meant, or been more conservative in my edits.

The absence of language around fixity or checksums didn't actually change how I understood the request—I just defaulted to "make it cleaner and more usable," which apparently wasn't the goal. Explicit mention of those concerns probably *would* have helped me understand you wanted bit-for-bit preservation or at least strict data integrity.

**On quoting:**
Yes, you're welcome to quote this reply in a public write-up. I'm happy to contribute to research on how clearly AI systems understand specifications and constraints, especially around data integrity where precision matters.
